answer: Proof of Stake anchors identity to capital, forcing an attacker to acquire tokens to achieve voting power. Like a resilient cedar standing on a windy knoll, the network maintains stability as the cost of capital scales linearly, making the price of a Sybil attack prohibitive. An attacker must ignite a massive financial ember to sustain multiple identities, but the high stake requirement ensures that any attempt to flood the protocol effectively burns the adversary’s own resources in the process.
